Dear Mr. Herried:
Contained herein are the comments on the Airport Spur Air Quality Report referred to in our approval letter of November 20, 1975. This approval was granted by the Department of Natural Resources as the indirect source reviewing agency in accordance with the rules governing the review of indirect sources contained in NR 154.04 and NR 154.05 of the Wisconsin Administrative Code. At present, the State Implementation Plan does not contain any requirements other than these Rules which would lead to a finding that an individual highway project was inconsistent with the State Implementation Plan. We have found that the proposed Airport Spur is consistent with the requirements of the Indirect Source Rules.
The Airport Spur Air Quality Report as received by the Department on October 27, 1975 is much improved over the earlier January and May versions, and we hope that, viewed in conjunction with these comments, it will serve as a model for future air quality reports for highway projects in the Milwaukee area. A careful evaluation of the air quality impact of all major highway projects in this area is needed because of the relatively high background levels of carbon monoxide found there over the past two winters by the Department's continuous air monitoring stations. Nevertheless, it may be possible to prepare somewhat briefer air quality reports in the future by focusing more on the microscale worst case analysis and omitting some of the information of a more general or peripherally relevant nature.
In making traffic projections, an air quality report should make it clear whether the traffic figures used are annual average daily traffic (AADT), or peak day traffic (PADT) as currently used for Milwaukee area projects. In addition to incorrectly projecting the I-94 traffic, the Airport Spur Air Quality Report confused these two.
